notes: Sources: 2018_01 CBA; 2018_02; 2018_03 (index page, no policy); 2018_04 (HR links page for OAs and unrepresented faculty, no policy text); 2018_05; 2018_06. 2018_07 (Faculty Handbook) is not used.

Governing document: the 2015-2018 UO-United Academics CBA (in force on the reference date; expires 2018-06-30). Art. 1 places all tenure-related faculty in the unit except supervisors, Law School and EC Cares faculty, so main-campus tenure-stream faculty are governed by it. Art. 6: ambiguity between University policies and the Agreement is resolved in favour of the Agreement.

The UO Parental Accommodation Policy (2018_05, 2010) predates the union; its text covers tenure-related and career NTTF faculty, but the HR site (2018_04) presents it for unrepresented faculty and 2018_02 presents the CBA for represented faculty. Its components (c21-c23) are coded for the unrepresented group and flagged ambiguous for review; for represented faculty the CBA provisions (c4-c7) are more generous (an employer-guaranteed six paid weeks) and cover the same ground.

The tenure-extension policy (2018_06) is coded as covering main-campus tenure-stream faculty (its text names regular tenure-related appointments; no saved document limits it to the unrepresented). It is discretionary, while the CBA gives represented faculty the option (c8, c9).

2018_02 (HR summary, undated) quotes both older CBA numbering (Art. 32 Secs. 8-10, including an eligibility clause naming 'Tenure-Track or Tenured Professor classifications' and a non-adverse-effect clause) and the 2015-18 text (Secs. 11-13). The CBA governs (source precedence); the older clauses add no leave or pay and are not components.

Statutory path: a member with two years' service meets FMLA (12 months, 1,250 hours) and OFLA (180 days; 25 hours a week for disability leave) eligibility (U8). CBA Art. 32 Sec. 10 restates FMLA and OFLA without adding length, so the leaves are coded as the statutes (c1-c3), with CBA pay within them.

OFLA ORS 659A.162(3)(a) pregnancy-disability leave (12 weeks, in addition to the 12 weeks of family leave) is relied on by CBA Sec. 11(c) ('qualify pursuant to the OFLA ... an additional 6 weeks'), so it is a component (U4, checklist C4) and OFLA parental leave follows it for the birth parent (S1a). The CBA's own 'third 6 weeks' (c6) is coded as sick-leave pay within that time.

Chain, birth parent: OFLA pregnancy-disability leave 12 (c3; FMLA c1 alongside from week 0) -> OFLA parental leave 12 (c2). Pay: CBA 11(a) 6 weeks full pay guaranteed by the employer after STD/vacation/sick balances (c4, within FMLA) -> 11(b) 6 weeks own sick leave or advance (c5) -> 11(c) up to 6 weeks own sick leave (c6). Modified duties up to one term at full pay, teaching relieved (c7), also_available after c4.
Chain, non-birth parent: FMLA 12 (c1) alongside OFLA parental leave 12 (c2). Pay: c4 6 weeks full pay -> c5 6 weeks own sick leave. Modified duties up to one term (c7), also_available after c4.

Calendar: the CBA uses 'terms' (three per academic year, Art. 33 Sec. 5(b)); 2018_05 refers to academic quarters and puts only the Law School on semesters. calendar.kind = quarter, and the term length follows R8's order.

Not components: Art. 32 Sec. 4 (pay not reduced for illnesses under five days for faculty below .5 FTE) excludes absences that qualify as FMLA/OFLA leave, so it cannot apply to a birth, and covers only faculty below .5 FTE; Art. 32 Sec. 23 paid winter and spring breaks (fixed calendar weeks, not a leave a parent takes); Art. 33 sabbatical (research purpose); Art. 34 jury duty; Art. 24 Sec. 7 administrative leave (disciplinary investigations); Art. 28 Sec. 5 child-care working group and Art. 32 Sec. 2 sick-leave-bank working group (studies, no benefit).
